clue.text: Contrapuntal music a college put on

parts.note: POLY is short for polytechnic, a kind of British college
something put on is fake or phony

explanation.surface: A college stages a performance of counterpoint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' reads as staged, but here it is an adjective meaning fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyphony is music woven from several independent melodic lines, which is what counterpoint is.

clue.text: Pair in black in story ready for publishing

indicators.note: the second in places the letter for black inside the word for story

parts.note: a story is a tale
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A couple feature in a dark tale that is now fit to go to press.
explanation.definitionFit: Copy that is fit to be printed is suitable for publication.

clue.text: Nobody's seed produces flower

explanation.surface: A man of no account produces a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nobody is Charles Pooter of the Grossmiths' comic novel 'The Diary of a Nobody', whose son is called Lupin.
explanation.definitionFit: Lupin Pooter is the son, or offspring, of the Nobody of the diary; separately the lupin is a garden plant with tall flower spikes.

clue.text: Person overtaking gets past non-stop traveller

parts.note: someone who overtakes another vehicle passes it, so is a passer
by can mean past, as in walking by the shop

explanation.surface: A motorist overtakes and speeds past someone travelling without a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes by without stopping is a pedestrian or traveller simply going past.

clue.text: Flood covering Florence, say

parts.note: over can mean covering, as in a lid over a pot

indicators.note: say signals that the short name is to be spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: Flo is a short form of the name Florence

explanation.surface: Floodwater covers the Italian city of Florence.
explanation.walkthrough: Florence looks like the Italian city, but it is the woman's name, shortened to FLO, which spoken sounds like FLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: To flood is to spill beyond the banks or brim.

clue.text: Sycophantic followers for head of state in republic

indicators.note: in places the first letter of state within the name of the republic

parts.note: Yemen is a republic in Arabia

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word state

explanation.surface: Fawning aides surround a head of state in some republic.
explanation.definitionFit: People who agree with everything the boss says are flattering hangers-on.

clue.text: Dishonest business producing additional growth

explanation.surface: A shady deal yields extra growth.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrupt dealing for profit is called graft; also a piece of tissue or a shoot spliced on to grow is a graft.

clue.text: Decrease to be recorded in warehouse

explanation.surface: A fall in stock is logged at the depot.
explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings: fall, be remembered (as in 'go down in history') and an Asian word for a storehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices go down when they fall; events go down in history when remembered; a godown is a storehouse in India and East Asia.

clue.text: Adding 100 to part of army in battle

indicators.note: in places the hundred and the army unit inside the fighting

parts.note: a battle is military action
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
RE are the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: A hundred soldiers from one unit join the fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Accretion is growth by gradual addition of layers or material.

clue.text: Tory replaced Liberal in holiday region

indicators.note: replaced signals that the letters of the word Tory are put back in a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal in politics

explanation.surface: In some resort area a Conservative ousted the Liberal candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyrol is an Alpine area of Austria and Italy popular for skiing and walking holidays.

clue.text: No hope of progress here, as has-been might say

explanation.surface: A washed-up figure laments being stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the word: someone whose time is over would say 'I'm passé'.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock is a situation with no way forward; a has-been is out of date, or passé.

clue.text: Cider as mixed in cocktail

indicators.note: mixed signals that the letters of cider and as are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Cider is blended into a mixed drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a cocktail of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice.

clue.text: Perfect, possibly? It's not easy

explanation.surface: Is flawlessness hard to achieve?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perfect' is the grammatical form, as in 'I have eaten', not flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: The perfect is one grammatical tense; someone not at ease is strained and nervous.

clue.text: Unimpeded spin to coast

parts.note: free means unimpeded, without hindrance
to wheel is to spin or turn round

explanation.surface: A cyclist spins along unhindered down to the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coast' looks like the seaside, but it is the verb meaning to move without pedalling.
explanation.definitionFit: To coast is to ride along without pedalling or power.

clue.text: Severe setback in main section? Blast!

parts.note: the body of something is its main part
a blast of wind is a blow

explanation.surface: Someone curses at a nasty setback in the main part of a project.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy punch to the torso is a figure for a serious misfortune.

clue.text: Follow and arrest band seen on Skye?

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
to collar a suspect is to arrest them

explanation.surface: Police tail and arrest a gang on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: Skye is a Scottish island, but said aloud it is 'sky': a cleric is a 'sky pilot' in slang, and the white band round a cleric's neck is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The stiff white collar worn by clergy is a band that marks a minister.

clue.text: Just off Oxford Street

explanation.surface: Close by a main road in Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: In Oxford the main street is known simply as 'the High'.
explanation.definitionFit: Game or meat just beginning to go off is said to be high; Oxford's High Street is called the High.

clue.text: Encouraging short story about a lost ship

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of short story and a are moved around

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: An uplifting short story about a ship that was lost at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' tells you SS goes: shuffling SHORT STORY and A without the two S's gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hortatory speech urges and exhorts, so it is meant to spur people on.

clue.text: What's running round garden? Pig, or another animal

parts.note: a hedge is a row of shrubs that runs round a garden's edge
a hog is a pig

explanation.surface: Something scampers round the garden: is it a pig or some other beast?
explanation.definitionFit: A hedgehog is a small spiny mammal, a creature distinct from the pig.

clue.text: Amount of drink an editor handled

parts.note: a finger is a measure of spirits, the depth of a finger's width in a glass

explanation.surface: An editor got a measure of whisky in their hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To finger something is to touch it with the hands.

clue.text: Advantage held by 17

indicators.note: held by means the letters sit inside the answer to clue 17

explanation.surface: A head start is kept by the spiny creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the edge over someone means being slightly ahead of them.

clue.text: Rookie's request to private

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so this reads rookie is

parts.note: to beg is to request
inner can mean private, as in one's inner thoughts

explanation.surface: A new recruit asks something of a private soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' looks like a soldier, but it is the adjective meaning personal.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is someone just starting out.

clue.text: Allow through an American university

parts.note: per means through or by means of, as in per post
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Permission is granted by an American college.
explanation.definitionFit: To permit is to let something happen.

clue.text: Bones found in ancient Turkish city

explanation.surface: Skeletal remains are dug up in an old city in Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsus is the group of ankle bones; Tarsus is also a historic city in southern Turkey, birthplace of St Paul.

clue.text: Report about what's inside Woomera — Aussie missile

indicators.note: about means the word for report goes round the middle part

parts.note: a report is a loud noise, a bang

indicators.note: what's inside means the letters of Woomera without its first and last

explanation.surface: A bang is heard from inside the Australian rocket range at Woomera.
explanation.walkthrough: Woomera is a rocket test range in South Australia, so the surface sets the scene for the missile.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved throwing stick of Aboriginal Australians is a returning missile.

clue.text: Very dear stuff, initially, in period of rising prices

indicators.note: in places the first letter of stuff within the economic period

parts.note: a boom is a time of economic growth and rising prices

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of the word stuff

explanation.surface: Precious goods appear at the start of an inflationary spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A bosom friend is a very close and cherished one.

clue.text: Old woman listened to letter from abroad

indicators.note: listened to means the word for old woman is heard, not read

parts.note: gammer is an old word for an elderly woman

explanation.surface: An elderly woman heard a letter from overseas being read out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' looks like correspondence, but it is a character of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamma is the third character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Parent's half-hearted stuff

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so this reads parent is

indicators.note: half-hearted means half of the central pair of letters is dropped

parts.note: matter is stuff, material

explanation.surface: A mother's things are only half-heartedly loved.
explanation.walkthrough: MATTER has a double T at its heart; losing one leaves the Latin word for mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Mater is Latin for mother, used in old-fashioned British slang for one's mum.

clue.text: Fare from Italy to southern Greek island

parts.note: salami is a spiced Italian sausage

explanation.surface: Food shipped from Italy to the south of Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Salamis is an island near Athens, site of a famous naval battle.

clue.text: Hard speech shortened in Shakespearean role

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: shortened means the word for speech loses its last letter

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A difficult speech is cut in a Shakespeare part.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio is Hamlet's loyal friend in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Revolutionary leader, in the long run, not honourable

indicators.note: not means the abbreviation for honourable is taken away

parts.note: a marathon is a long-distance race

explanation.surface: A rebel chief, over time, proves dishonourable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the long run' reads as eventually, but it is a marathon.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Paul Marat was a leading radical of the French Revolution.

clue.text: Artist returned half of 3's cheese

indicators.note: returned means the painter's name is read backwards

parts.note: Degas was a French painter

indicators.note: half of means only the second half of the answer to clue 3 is kept

parts.note: refers to the answer to clue 3

explanation.surface: A painter went back to a piece of cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns DEGAS into SAGED; 'half of' keeps ERBY, the back half of PASSERBY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage Derby is an English cheese marbled green with sage.
